title: C24/72/2019 of SHWETA AGARWAL Vs MANISH AGARWAL

paras.text:
C24 No.72 of 2019
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.

Mr. Mohd. Azim, Advocate for the
applicant.
 Mr. Pankaj Kumar, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for
the respondent.
 Heard.
 By means of present civil transfer
application, moved under Section 24 of CPC,
applicant is seeking transfer of O.S.
No.171/2019 Manish Agarwal vs. Smt.
Shweta Agarwal, under Section 13(1) of
Hindu Marriage Act, pending before the
Additional Family Judge, Rishikesh, District
Dehradun to the court of Family Court,
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
 The case of the applicant is that the
marriage of the applicant and respondent
was solemnized on 20.4.2014. After the
marriage, she was tortured for demand of
dowry by the respondent and in July 2017
she was ousted from the matrimonial house
for not fulfilling the demand of dowry. Out of
the wedlock, a daughter was born, however,
the respondent while ousting the applicant
from the house, forcibly kept the daughter
with him.
 Ground shown for transfer is that the
applicant is doing computer course at
Jaspur and is presently residing in a
tenanted accommodation at Jaspur. Besides
this, it is also stated that the applicant is a
poor lady and has no source of income, she
is financially dependent upon her parents
and, in such circumstances, it is very
difficult for her to travel from Jaspur to
Rishikesh to attend court proceedings in
Rishikesh.
 Respondent has filed objections to the
transfer application denying the averments
made in the transfer application. It is also
stated that the applicant has left the
matrimonial house and minor child with her
own will.
 Having heard learned counsel for the
parties and after perusal of affidavit as well

as the counter affidavit, this Court is of the
considered view that the applicant has failed
to make out a case for transfer of aforesaid
case. There is no merit in the present
transfer application. Same is hereby
dismissed.
